_comment: Bundled-tool sources. Two ways a tool lands on the drive: (1) STAGING - you download it once from the vendor page into a folder and pass -StagingDir; Build-Kit finds it by staging_glob, copies/extracts it, and logs its SHA-256. (2) URL - Build-Kit fetches automatically (following redirects, sending a browser user-agent). Staging always wins when both are present, so staging remains the override for any URL that rots. Most tools now auto-fetch; three (smartmontools, emsisoft, windbg) are STAGING ONLY because their only download is an installer/SFX that needs extraction Build-Kit doesn't perform - their _note has the steps. Checksum rule: a VERSION-PINNED url (the version is in the path) carries a real pinned sha256 - when the vendor bumps the version the old url 404s and Build-Kit skips it gracefully, so the pin never causes a false mismatch abort; a ROLLING/unversioned url (or a non-byte-stable GitHub archive) uses sha256:'unpinned' with an _unpinned_reason, because the bytes change in place under a fixed url and a pin would hard-fail the build on the vendor's next refresh - Build-Kit logs the actual hash it shipped. An optional 'filename' names the local download when the url carries no usable extension (so a bare .exe is copied, not mistaken for an archive). See GET-TOOLS.md for the staging-only tools and version bumps.

tools.name: sysinternals-suite
tools._unpinned_reason: Microsoft ships the whole Sysinternals Suite from one stable, unversioned URL and refreshes individual tools in place, so the archive's bytes change on any tool update and a pinned hash would abort the build on Microsoft's next refresh. Build-Kit logs the actual SHA-256 of the copy it ships.
tools._note: Auto-fetches from the stable URL. (Previously had an empty sha256, which made Build-Kit skip it; 'unpinned' is the correct marker for a rolling-in-place URL.) sdelete*.exe is removed post-extract (not whitelisted).

tools.name: microsoft-safety-scanner
tools._unpinned_reason: MSERT bundles its own malware signatures and expires ~10 days after download, so the binary legitimately differs on every build and a pinned hash would always be stale. Build-Kit logs the actual SHA-256 of the copy it ships.
tools._note: 64-bit MSERT. Auto-fetches via the fwlink (no extension in the URL, so 'filename' forces msert.exe rather than an extension-less copy). Stage a msert.exe to override.

tools.name: adwcleaner
tools._unpinned_reason: Malwarebytes serves the latest AdwCleaner build from one unversioned URL (302 -> CDN), so the binary changes silently release-to-release and a pinned hash would abort the build on every vendor update without a URL change to signal it. Build-Kit logs the actual SHA-256 of the copy it ships. URL has no extension; 'filename' names the output and Content-Disposition confirms adwcleaner.exe.
tools._note: Auto-fetches the current portable adwcleaner.exe (verified ready-to-run PE32). Stage an adwcleaner*.exe to override/pin.

tools.name: emsisoft-emergency-kit
tools._note: STAGING ONLY - not auto-fetched. The download (https://dl.emsisoft.com/EmsisoftEmergencyKit.exe, ~319 MB, refreshed daily) is a 7-Zip SFX, and the kit needs the EXTRACTED tree (Run\a2cmd.exe), not the SFX itself - Build-Kit does not run installers. Extract on the build machine ('7z x EmsisoftEmergencyKit.exe -oC:\EEK -y', or run it once to unpack to C:\EEK), then place that EEK folder in staging named 'emsisoft'. a2cmd.exe still needs an online signature update on first use ('a2cmd /u'). GET-TOOLS.md has the steps.

tools.name: bleachbit-portable
tools._note: Auto-fetches BleachBit 6.0.2 portable. SHA-256 matches the vendor's published sha256sum.txt exactly. Zip wraps a single 'BleachBit-Portable\' folder; Build-Kit flattens it so the binary lands at tools\bleachbit\bleachbit_console.exe as the playbook expects. Version-pinned URL: when BleachBit ships a new release this URL 404s (Build-Kit skips gracefully) - bump the url+sha256 to the current portable zip (its hash is at download.bleachbit.org/bleachbit-<ver>-sha256sum.txt) or stage it. Do NOT use the /get/ path - it serves an HTML interstitial.

tools.name: wiztree-portable
tools._note: Auto-fetches WizTree 4.32 portable (301-redirects to a CDN; Build-Kit follows it). Extracts WizTree64.exe (and 32-bit WizTree.exe) at the root. Version-pinned URL: bump url+sha256 on a new WizTree release, or stage the current portable zip.

tools.name: smartmontools
tools._note: STAGING ONLY - not auto-fetchable to a portable binary. Every official Windows build (SourceForge 7.5 and builds.smartmontools.org) ships ONLY the NSIS installer smartmontools-7.5.win32-setup.exe, never a bare smartctl.exe. Extract it on the build machine with 7-Zip ('7z x smartmontools-7.5.win32-setup.exe' -> bin\smartctl.exe) or silent-install ('...setup.exe /S' then copy from %ProgramFiles%\smartmontools\bin\), and stage smartctl.exe (+ its DLLs). GET-TOOLS.md has the steps. Installer URL for reference: https://sourceforge.net/projects/smartmontools/files/smartmontools/7.5/smartmontools-7.5.win32-setup.exe/download

tools.name: speedtest-cli
tools._note: Auto-fetches Ookla Speedtest CLI 1.2.0 (win64). Extracts speedtest.exe at the root. Version-pinned URL: bump url+sha256 on a new release, or stage the current win64 zip. RUNTIME NOTE for the repair agent: speedtest.exe blocks on an interactive license/GDPR prompt on first run - it must be invoked with '--accept-license --accept-gdpr'.

tools.name: nirsoft-bluescreenview
tools._unpinned_reason: NirSoft rebuilds BlueScreenView in place under one unversioned URL, so the zip's bytes change silently between releases and a pinned hash would abort the build on the vendor's next rebuild. Build-Kit logs the actual SHA-256 of the copy it ships. (NirSoft rejects empty/scripted user-agents; Build-Kit sends a browser UA.)
tools._note: Auto-fetches the 64-bit BlueScreenView (extracts BlueScreenView.exe). Add other NirSoft zips to staging with matching globs if you extend the whitelist.

tools.name: snappy-driver-installer-origin
tools._note: Auto-fetches SDIO 2.0.3.886 (the tool only, ~11.7 MB - launchers SDIO_x64_R886.exe / SDIO_R886.exe; it downloads driverpack indexes at runtime). Version-pinned URL with no 'latest' alias: bump url+sha256 on a new SDIO release, or stage the current zip. For OFFLINE NIC recovery you still stage the NETWORK driverpack (drivers\DP_*LAN*/*WLAN*) into staging\SDIO yourself - that is not auto-fetched (full packs are tens of GB; network-only is a few hundred MB).

tools.name: windows-debugging-tools-cdb
tools._note: STAGING ONLY - not auto-fetchable. There is no direct URL to cdb.exe; the only download is the 1.45 MB SDK bootstrapper winsdksetup.exe (current: https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2376217, SDK 10.0.28000.2705), which pulls the debugger MSIs at install time. On the build machine run 'winsdksetup.exe /features OptionId.WindowsDesktopDebuggers /quiet' (or '/layout <dir>' offline), then copy C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Debuggers\x64\ (cdb.exe + its sibling DLLs dbgeng.dll/dbghelp.dll) into staging named 'windbg' (a folder). Optional / heaviest - skip for a first full build.

tools.name: win11debloat
tools._unpinned_reason: GitHub's /archive/refs/tags/<tag>.zip is generated on demand and is NOT byte-stable - GitHub has changed archive compression before, so the same tag can hash differently over time. Pinning would risk a false mismatch abort. Build-Kit logs the actual SHA-256 of the copy it ships. (This repo uses date tags with no 'v' prefix, e.g. 2026.08.24.)
tools._note: Auto-fetches the pinned release source zip. The archive wraps a single Win11Debloat-2026.08.24\ folder; Build-Kit flattens it so Win11Debloat.ps1 lands at tools\win11debloat\Win11Debloat.ps1. Bump the tag in the url to move releases. There are no release-asset zips - the source archive IS the artifact.

tools.name: oo-shutup10
tools._unpinned_reason: O&O serves the latest OOSU10.exe from one stable, unversioned path and refreshes it in place, so the binary changes silently between releases and a pinned hash would abort the build on the vendor's next refresh. Build-Kit logs the actual SHA-256 of the copy it ships.
tools._note: Auto-fetches the single portable OOSU10.exe (~76 MB, runs directly). 'filename' forces the .exe extension so it is copied, not treated as an archive. Add your curated 'recommended.cfg' to staging too if you want a default profile shipped.
